subject: forestSpirit
reasoning:
I'm designing a forest spirit for the module—a tall, gnarled figure with root-like legs, a mossy cloak, a deer-skull mask with antlers, glowing eyes, and floating leaf wisps, planning out the skeleton structure to build it with the SDK.

Mapping out the joint hierarchy...

Writing finger sprout logic...

Now for the torso, I'm planning a sweep over the spine chain with a tapered radius function going from hips to chest, and defining a bark paint combining grain and mottle textures for the color.

For the legs, I'll use sweeps along leg chains with a decreasing radius array, applying the bark paint. For the head, I'm thinking of an elongated skull shape using a scaled sphere geometry with a pale color tone.

Still building the head geometry...

Designing the antler branches as a curved beam with tapering radius using swept polyline points, with smaller rod tines branching off at specific points along the beam, plus maybe tiny leaf cards for detail.

For the leaves, I'm scattering hit points across the torso/skirt surface and placing textured leaf cards there, filtering by surface normal direction and varying size, lean, and spin for natural randomness. Writing the leaf SVG texture...

For the cloak or skirt, I'm sketching out a lathe-based ragged moss skirt around the hips, defining a jagged profile outline with low segment count for a flat low-poly look, colored with moss paint.

For shoulder decoration, I'm adding a moss mantle plus a few tiny mushrooms on the right shoulder using hemisphere caps in a reddish-orange colored stem pairing.

For the tail, I'm chaining a few bone points from the hips backward into a tapered leafy sweep colored like moss, ending with a small glowing orb at the tip, and considering a few floating wisp spheres nearby for extra flair.

Now I'm figuring out the toes: three small capsules per foot branching from the ankle joint, sized and positioned so they taper down and just touch the floor without clipping through it.

Moving up, I'm shaping the torso with a sweeping radius profile along the spine chain, adding a chest bulge, then transitioning into a tapered neck sweep that connects at the same joint position as the chest tip.

Now I'm placing a small glowing green orb on the chest to act as a heart light, then building the arms with tapering sweep radii down to the wrist, adding a palm sphere and three small finger tips spread outward with slight offsets.

Setting up the limb chains with named bones for shoulder, elbow, wrist on the arms and hip, knee, ankle on the legs, all parented under the chest or torso root. I'm also surfacing bark-textured card scatter across the torso and limb bones using the sweep meshes, and adding simple facial details like brow ridges, nose holes, and small spike-shaped ear leaves jutting from the back of the head.

I'm mottling the skull paint with a muted bone-and-tan texture, adding dark eye socket spheres and thin green cheek marks for variation, then mirroring all these features left-to-right using a signed loop. I'm settling on roughly 2.2-2.45 meters tall including antlers, which feels right for a spirit creature, and now moving into writing the antler geometry using swept polylines along defined control points.

Writing antler sweep code...
